verdict.rationale: Lambda's own docs say instances can be launched and restarted through the Lambda Cloud REST API, a probe confirms the provisioning API is live, and on-demand instances are billed hourly in one-minute increments. However, nothing documents a stop/start (pause) action, and first-party terminate is evidenced only indirectly, through a third-party CLI that uses the API. Community reports confirm billing runs for as long as an instance is running, so the only cost control evidenced is terminating it. missing for 10: documented programmatic stop/start (pause), first-party documentation of the terminate endpoint, evidence that stopped instances stop accruing compute charges.

support.subject: As a developer, I can start, stop, restart, and terminate instances programmatically and keep paying only for what is running

citations.quote: You can also launch instances programmatically by using the Lambda Cloud API.
You can also restart instances programmatically by using the Lambda Cloud API.
The Lambda Cloud API provides a set of REST API endpoints you can use to create and manage your Lambda Cloud resources.
ODC prices instances by hourly usage and bills in one-minute increments.
